about: A stored record's list (order.lines) loads with the record, one level deep, by the one reference of each listed record back to it (docs/ledger/runtime-data.md, step 2). A find loads each list with one read for all the records it found, `ownersPerRead` owners at a time (well below the fewest parameters a database takes in one statement, SQL Server's 2100), and gives each record exactly its own items, in the order they were stored; never one read per record. A case saves `orders` orders (ids 1 to `orders`), then its `lines` in their order, each `[order, product]` (an order beyond `orders` was not asked for), finds the orders, and expects each order named in `expect` to hold the products given, and the lines to be read `reads` times.
